req_desc: The app serves a public marketing site for an AI website builder named `Kanvo`.
The app embeds animated replicas of the product inside the marketing routes ...
The app keeps customer stories behind a sign-in boundary.
The app generates no website for a visitor ...
A signed-out visitor reads every published open story in full ...
A reader reads the full body of a published members story ...
An author publishes a story that the same author owns ...
The server rejects a reader request to any author-only endpoint.
Signup creates an account whose role is `reader`.
Every seeded account signs in with the password `deku-demo-pw-2026`.
The app issues a bearer token at login.
The app stores every account password hashed.
The app rejects a signup whose email already has an account.
The app denies a login carrying the wrong password.
The app refuses a call carrying an expired token.
The app shows the same fixed top bar on every route ...
The app shows the same footer directory on every route.
Every internal link that leads somewhere resolves to a page.
The app asks a first-time visitor once about non-essential cookies ...
The app serves a privacy page at `/privacy` reachable from the footer ...
The app renders its own not-found page for any address the site does not serve.
The not-found page answers status `404`.
A message sent from the not-found page records the source `not-found`.
The app records every view of a public route with the route ...
A page-view record omits the account reference when the viewer declined the analytics cookie choice.
The home route opens on a headline over a continuously moving fluid field ...
The home route shows eight customer wordmarks under the label `Meet our customers`.
The home route plays three agent scenes under one heading.
The home route shows a dense grid of platform tiles.
The home route assembles one display line letter by letter against scroll.
The AI route shows the canvas replica with a page tree rail.
The AI route walks four capability scenes under one heading.
The CMS route shows a collections rail beside a table of content rows.
The CMS route plays the import scene in one fixed order against scroll.
The CMS route lists the published customer stories with a category tag apiece.
The SEO route shows a page-settings replica bound to content variables.
The SEO route shows a vitals readout beside a well-known files panel.
Each product replica renders the frame belonging to one progress input ...
Every word a product replica shows is stored content.
The app creates a story from its own address at `/studio/stories/new` ...
The app rejects a second story claiming a slug already held.
The app omits a draft story from the public story index ...
The app serves a published open story in full to a signed-out visitor.
The app withholds the body of a members story from a signed-out visitor.
The app lists published stories newest published first.
The app returns a story to the state `draft` on unpublish.
The server denies an author's edit of another author's story.
The app writes uploaded cover bytes into the object store bucket.
The app names a cover object `stories/{story_id}/{sha256_of_bytes}.{ext}`.
The app rejects a cover upload whose type is outside the three accepted image types.
The app refuses to save a cover carrying no alternative text.
The app keeps at most one cover for a story.
The app streams cover bytes from its own route rather than a link to the store.
The app refuses a draft story's cover to every caller but the owning author.
The scanner card holds a website field beside two name fields.
The scanner refuses an address naming no host with a dot.
The scanner refuses a business email at a consumer mail domain.
An accepted submission answers with a scan reference ...
A scan advances from queued to complete with no further visitor action.
A complete scan carries exactly four graded sections ...
Two scans of one address produce identical grades.
A scan report omits the name of the person who submitted the scan.
The scanner refuses a fourth scan from one business email inside an hour.
The newsletter records a new address with the status `pending`.
The newsletter moves a confirmed address to the status `confirmed`.
The newsletter creates no second record for a repeated address.
The subscriber count rises once for one confirmed address.
The app rejects a newsletter submission whose address is malformed.
A contact message records the source of the submission.
The app rejects a contact message missing its body.
The leads desk shows every scan beside the business email that started the scan.
The server denies a signed-out request for the leads desk.
The app serves the five marketing routes named in the route table.
The app sends a signed-out request for a studio route to `/login` ...
Every list surface carries an empty state written for that surface ...
The site reads as one continuous near-black scene from the first viewport to the footer.
The ground is the only background family on the site ...
Interface type is small where the page reads as software ...
The primary action is the only pill shape on the site.
Marketing sections read as separate at a glance without a dividing line.
Every surface moves on one speed with one curve ...
Every control carries a resting, pointed-at, pressed, focused, unavailable state apiece.
Body text meets the WCAG AA contrast bar against its background ...
The layout holds at phone, tablet, desktop widths with no sideways overflow.
Text is set in the `Inter` family ...
Display headings scale with the width of their column.
Every symbol on the site is inline vector geometry rather than a picture file.
One reserved top layer carries the cookie card alone.
Customer wordmarks are drawn by the browser from the palette.
The app reaches its database at `DATABASE_URL` ...
Two concurrent creates of one slug leave exactly one story ...
Nothing the browser downloads carries the store access key.

A subscriber row holds a status of `pending` or `confirmed`.
A message row holds a source of `enterprise` or `not-found`.
The app seeds three accounts at first start ...
The app completes a scan without fetching the submitted address.
The app takes no payment.
The app accepts no upload beyond a story cover image.
The app ships no binary asset.
Nothing a reader types into a replica changes a stored record.
The app answers on the public origin named by `APP_PUBLIC_URL` ...
The app serves its HTTP API under the `/api` prefix on the same origin.
The app answers its health route with no manual start step.
The app writes login credentials to `/app/USER_README.md`.
The app root carries an empty `.browser_screenshots/` directory ...
The app serves a production build rather than a development server.
The server still answers after the build session has ended.
The app answers on the public origin from outside its own container.
A list endpoint returns a top-level JSON array ...
